name: Rick Wilson
blurb: Former Republican ad man, writing daily politics against the party he used to make commercials for.

name: Matt Kiser
site: What The Fuck Just Happened Today?
blurb: One post a day, seven numbered items, every one sourced. He has kept this up since 2017, which is the part I find hard to believe.

name: Kylie Bodiya
blurb: Disney shirts and art prints built on deep cuts instead of character faces. She writes about running the business as openly as she designs for it.

name: Casey Newton
blurb: AI and the social platforms. He left a big publication to report on them independently.

name: Matthew Haughey
blurb: Projects, places, and useful obsessions — woodworking, bikes, home automation. He built MetaFilter, and has been posting here since 1999.

name: Mike Monteiro
blurb: A designer with strong opinions about what designers owe people. One reader question a week, and only if he thinks he can answer it well.

name: Joanna Stern
blurb: Consumer tech reviewed by someone who is funny about it. Foldables, doorbell cameras, whatever Apple just shipped.

name: Julia Evans
blurb: Explains how computer things work, DNS and git and the shell, without pretending you already knew. Her Wizard Zines are the illustrated version.

name: Josh Barro and Ken White
blurb: An irreverent podcast about the law, which mostly means a defense lawyer explaining why the case you read about is not the case you think it is.

name: Cassidy Williams
blurb: Developer advocacy at GitHub, plus a weekly newsletter with an interview question in it. A lot of the memes in my feed start here.

name: Georgia Dunn
blurb: A syndicated comic strip where the household cats are a news crew reporting on their own house. Based on her actual cats.

name: FueledbyLOLZ
blurb: Race recaps, shoe reviews, and diner reviews from a runner in California. Never signs a name to any of it.

name: Dan Hon
blurb: Technology, government, and design, tangled up with ADHD and fatherhood and being an immigrant here. Running since 2014 and past a million words.

name: j.b. crawford
blurb: The history of the computer and telecom industry, with a fondness for its stranger bit players. He writes it to explain why computers are the way they are.

name: Ana Marie Cox
blurb: Founded Wonkette, then spent two decades in political media. Now she writes about craft and runs workshops on it.

name: Patrick Wardle
blurb: Free, open-source Mac security tools, plus malware analysis written up in detail. If you run a Mac, install a few of these.

name: Amelia Boone
blurb: Obstacle racing champion, ultrarunner, attorney. Writes about injury and recovery and aging with more candor than the genre usually allows. Night Owl Studio built this site.

name: Patrick McKenzie
blurb: Monthly essays on how financial infrastructure works underneath the app: card networks, fraud, the plumbing nobody explains.
